previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with severe hyperglycemia in the setting of dexamethasone therapy for a pathologic spinal fracture related to multiple myeloma. His blood glucose reached the 400s despite adherence to his home insulin regimen. He also presented with acute kidney injury, likely due to volume depletion, and a history of recurrent falls attributed to diabetic neuropathy and deconditioning from a prior prolonged hospitalization. During admission, his blood sugar improved with insulin adjustment and his renal function normalized with IV fluids. An endocrinology recommendation was implemented to increase his basal and bolus insulin on steroid days. He remained stable, with no infectious complications, and was discharged home with physical therapy for fall prevention and plans for outpatient follow-up with his endocrinologist, oncologist, and primary care provider.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ y/o with MM s/p auto SCT now with recurrence, on Revlimid, 
who presents after fall, found to be confused and with a fever 
to 101.
.
# Metabolic Encephalopathy: Initial presenation consisted of 
intermittent confusion although pt was AAOx3, inattentiveness, 
hand to finger dysmetria, slurring of speech, and asterixis. 
Reports of dehydration and hypoglycemia, per EMS/ED. Febrile in 
ED to 101 but no recorded fever while admitted. CT ___ was 
negative for intercranial bleed and on repeat CT ___ 24 hours 
later (looking for delayed bleed). Ruled out 
encephalitis/meningitis with an LP (only 1 WBC) on the first day 
of admission, and normal MRI. Negative CSF microbiology studies. 
Blood/Urine cxs were negative. No evidence of CVA on MRI. EEG 
was negative for seizure. Consideration was made for EtOH 
withdrawal/___. Serum EtOH negative x2 on 
admission; tox screen also negative for illcit drugs. Also did 
not respond to Diazepam for hypertension during admission (see 
HTN below). Given h/o EtOH abuse and reports from wife of EtOH 
use, pt was started on high dose IV Thiamine x3days and 
eventually transitioned to PO Thiamine. Patient was transiently 
on Acyclovir IV for HSV until CSF PCR returned negative. Was 
never on antibiotics (other then x1 doses of Vanco/Cefepime 
given in ED). It was thought that the patient presented with 
metabolic encephalopthy 2/t dehydration, hypoglycemia, 
polypharmacy (takes numerous anti-cholinergic and sedating drugs 
at home), hypertensive encephalopathy, and EtOH use (w/ possible 
___). Neurology/ID was following pt and agreed 
that the presenation was likely 2/t metabolic encephalopathy 
after reviewing the data. Slowly improved without antibiotics or 
any other intervention besides that of IV Thiamine and limiting 
sedating/anti-cholinergic drugs. Prior to discharge, pt was 
found to be back at his baseline. Medication reconciliation was 
done and his list was narrowed to only essential medications.
.
# Fever on Admission: Spiked to 101 in ED. Recieved 
Vanco/Cefepime in the ED. No localizing infectious symptoms but 
endorsed confusion/malaise on admission. No HA, photophobia, 
neck pain to suggest meningitis. Confusion with fever suggested 
encephalitis, such as HSV encephalitis. CXR wnl. Received 
Vanco/Zosyn x1 in the ED. LP revealed only one WBC on 
differential which reduced our suspicion for CNS infection; MRI 
also without signs of infection. Cultures ultimately returned 
negative. Did not recieve antibiotics while admitted but was 
kept on IV Acyclovir until HSV PCR returned negative. No fevers 
during the admission while off antibiotics. Repeat CXR after 
fluids (~3days) did not reveal a PNA.
.
# Cough: Developed on ___, productive of brown sputum, 
without fevers or SOB. CXR suggested a LLL opacity. Decisionw 
was made to pursue a CTA given known DVT in ___ and ___ with 
evidence of new pulmonary HTN. CTA showed multiple R sided PEs, 
unclear exact acuity. Started on Levofloxacin x7d for community 
acquired pneumonia. Pt likely qualified for HCAP but givne no 
fever or SOB, watched him on Levofloxacin with th eplan to 
broaden if febrile or worsening symptoms. Pt quickly responded 
to Levofloxacin and cough improved after one day. Cough could 
have also been possibly due to infarction 2/t PEs. Sputum cx was 
insufficient x2.
.
# PE: Multiple right-sided PEs, likely from known DVT but 
difficult to determine exact acuity given that he was never 
tachycardic, hypoxic, or complaining of SOB. Unclear if caused 
initial presentation of AMS. ___ done during this admission 
showed new pulm htn, suggesting possible chronicity. Pt does 
have a h/o b/l PEs ___ years ago. On admission, patient was 
supratherapeutic on both Coumadin/Lovenox. Anticoagulation 
reversed for 12 hours for LP with resumption of anti-coagulation 
4 hours after procedure. Lovenox was eventually switched to 
Arixtra given concenr for HIT - eventually returned negative. 
Hypercoagulable work-up was unrevealing. Will likely need 
lifetime anti-coagulation, should be considered for trnasition 
to Warfarin as an outpt. 
.
# R ___ DVT: Recently diagnosed DVT in ___ by PCP. Apparent 
large burden from reports obtained from Atrius. Confirmed clot 
with US during this admission - right distal femoral and 
popliteal veins. INR transiently reversed for LP and quickly 
restarted on anticoagulation 4 hours after procedure. Complained 
of posterior back pain controlled with meds/lidocaine patches. 
No signs of distal emboli during admission; never 
tachycardic/hypoxic or complained of SOB. No respiratory 
distress during admission. As an outpt, pt was receiving Lovenox 
as a bridging to Warfarin. Initially continued on Lovenox. 
Eventually decision was made to switch to Arixtra given concern 
for HIT (ultimately returned negative). DVT slowly improving at 
time of discharge. Discharged on Arixtra. Consideration should 
be made for starting Warfarin as an outpt.
.
# Coagulopathy: Elevated ___ on admission. High fibrinogen, 
which did not suggest DIC. Likely 2/t recent use of concurrent 
warfarin/lovenox while pt was being treated for DVT as outpt. 
INR reversed for LP. Restarted anticoagulation for DVT 4 hours 
after LP. Smear without evidence of TTP/DIC.
.
# HTN: Was hypertensive at time of admission, which was likely 
contributing to the presentation of encephalopathy. No CVA on 
MRI but with evidence of chronic microangiopathy. Smear did not 
show evidence of TTP. Trialed Diazepam early in the admission 
due to a suspicion of EtOH WD to no effect, actually made the 
patient more encephalopathic. Initially trialed on home meds of 
Atenolol to no effect. Switched to Lebatalol which was titrated 
up. Home Amlodipine was also eventually started. BP slowly 
improved. Unclear etiology for the uncontrolled HTN given well 
controlled BPs in clinic. Secondary causes of HTN were 
investigated, however, TSH and cortisol wnl. Renal US did not 
show significant renovascular disease. ___ in ___ showed mild 
MR and no LVH. Repeat ___ showed new pulmonary HTN, dilated 
atria, LVH, and worsened MR - However, these findings did not 
help elucidate an acute cause of an elevation in BP. Vasculitic 
workup was also unrevealing with negative ___, ANCA, and RF. 
Cardiology was consulted and followed the patient. BP at time of 
discharge was better controlled on Lebetalol and Amlodipine.
.
# MM: S/p auto SCT in ___. On Revlimaid therapy as an outpt. 
With recurrence given increase in IgA but currently well 
controlled with most recent IgA of 351 during this admission. 
Also s/p XRT for a vertebral fx. Anemia/Thrombocytopenia likely 
2/t this process. Revlimid was held during admission. Cytology 
of CSF did not show malignant cells. Continued acyclovir ppx. 
During the admission, pt required blood transfusions for hct 
below 21, platelets were also lower compared to previous results 
(now below 100). Initial concern was for TTP/DIC given no prior 
transfusion requirements. Smear was unrvealing and firbinogen 
was elevated. No signs of hemolysis on labs. Given low platelets 
and anemia, HIT was suspected given recent initiation fo 
Lovenox. Switched to Arixtra given this concern. HIT antibody 
returned negative. PICC (placed due to difficult stick, R arm) 
also was not working properly during the admission, at times 
requiring TPA daily, and thus lab values may have been 
inaccurate. Peripheral lab draw had an H/H of ___ but plts 
were also low in the ___. Ultimately, pt underwent a bone marrow 
biopsy for evaluation of marrow given low reticulocyte count. 
There is concern that he has developed a new marrow pathology 
leading to suppressed counts, nonsecretory MM (given that 
current IgA is not very elevated). Another consideration id drug 
induced marrow suppression. Initial core evaluation was 
unremarkable. Final bone marrow biopsy is pending. Given 
suppressed counts, Revlamid was held on discharge and can be 
considered for reinitiation as an outpt once counts improve. 
Close follow-up and labs draws were arranged prior to discharge.
.
# EtOH Abuse: Reports of EtOH abuse in previous documentation. 
Wife reported heavy alcohol use - 1 galloon per day of liquor. 
Unclear if this quantification was accurate, serum EtOH negative 
x2 on admission. Given possible risk of withdrawal with these 
reports, pt was started on CIWA and diazepam prn. Did not have 
classic symptoms of withdrawal and was never given Diazepam per 
CIWA. Was trialed on Diazepam for HTN early in admission to no 
effect. Given the reports of EtOH use and AMS, pt was started on 
high dose IV Thiamine x3days and eventually transitioned to PO 
Thiamine for possible Wernicke Korsakoff syndrome. Psychiatry 
and SW followed the patient during admission. Emphasis was made 
on the importance of abstaining from EtOH use given medication 
interaction. A alcohol group appointment was made prior to 
discharge. Discharged on PO Thiamine. 
.
# Peripheral Neuropathy: Continued Gabapentin at a lower dose of 
300mg PO TID. Held Duloxetine. Held Amitryptiline. Stopped 
oxycontin. Did not complain of neuropathic pain during 
admission. As a result, d/c Amitriptyline, Oxycontin, Duloxetine 
in order to simplify drug regimen and prevent future drug 
interactions given presentation of metabolic encephalopathy.
.
# DM: Started on reduced ISS given presentation with 
hypoglycemia. Blood sugars well controlled on only short acting 
insulin. Never given Lantus during admission. Likely 2/t having 
a set diabetic diet. Instructed to monitor blood sugars at home 
and start Lantus if needed.
.
# Hep B: Continued Lamvudine.
.

FINDINGS:

likely the sequelae of chronic microangiopathy, not significantly changed
since the prior examination of ___, but slightly more progressed since

TECHNIQUE:  Contiguous axial MDCT images were obtained through the chest after
the administration of IV contrast per the chest pain protocol.  Sagittal,
coronal, and maximum intensity projection oblique reformatted images were
obtained and reviewed.

FINDINGS:  There is a small 5-mm hypodensity in the left lobe of the thyroid
gland.  The thyroid gland is otherwise unremarkable.  There is no axillary,
mediastinal, or hilar lymphadenopathy.  Small scattered mediastinal and hilar
lymph nodes do not meet criteria for pathologic enlargement, and are unchanged
from the prior exam.  There is an enlarged right paraesophageal lymph node
which measures 11 mm, and is unchanged from the prior exam.  The esophagus is
normal without wall thickening or dilation.  There is no hiatal hernia.

The heart is normal in size.  Trace pericardial fluid is likely physiologic. 
There is no significant atherosclerotic disease in the coronary arteries along
the aortic valve.  There is no CT evidence of right heart strain.  The
thoracic aorta is normal in course and caliber.  The main pulmonary artery
trunk diameter is at the upper limits of normal.

There is a pulmonary embolism at the bifurcation of the right upper and middle
segmental pulmonary arteries.  Additionally, there are multiple pulmonary
embolisms in the right lower segmental and subsegmental pulmonary artery
branches.  There are no pulmonary emboli identified within the left pulmonary
arteries.

The airways are patent to the subsegmental levels.  There are no endobronchial
lesions.  Evaluation of the pulmonary parenchyma is somewhat limited by
respiratory motion.  At the right base, there is an ill-defined consolidation
within surrounding ground-glass which is nonspecific.  Given its proximity to
the right lower lobe pulmonary emboli, it may represent an early infarction
though infection is a consideration.  In the left lower lobe, there is a
similar opacitiy, with a more linear configuration.  There are no discrete
nodules, though again evaluation is limited by respiratory motion.  There is
no pleural effusion or pneumothorax.

This exam is not tailored to evaluate the subdiaphragmatic structures.  Within
the limitations, the imaged portions of the liver, spleen, adrenal glands, and
stomach are unremarkable.

There is a partially imaged compression fracture of T12 (401B, 43), which is
unchanged from the lumbar spine CT for ___.  This is most likely
pathologic.  No other fracture is identified.  No lytic or sclerotic lesions
are identified elsewhere in the thorax.  There is unchanged irregularity of
the sternomanubrial joint, likely from a prior infection.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Multiple segmental and subsegmental pulmonary emboli involving the right
upper, middle, and lower pulmonary arteries.  No pulmonary emboli within the
left pulmonary arteries.  No CT evidence of right heart strain.
2.  Bilateral lower lobe consolidations, which are nonspecific.  The
differential diagnosis includes early infarction related to the pulmonary
emboli or pneumonia.  Atelectasis is also a possibility, though less likely.
3.  Unchanged appearance of a pathologic T12 compression fracture.  No new
fracture or osseous lesion is identified.

PELVIS:  The patient is status post prostatectomy.  The bladder is
unremarkable.  There is no free fluid in the pelvis.  There is no pelvic

BONES AND SOFT TISSUES:  Once again, there are unusual dystrophic
calcifications superior to the pubic symphysis bilaterally which track along
the fascial planes; however, this is unchanged from multiple prior studies. 
Multiple soft tissue and areas of soft tissue changes along the anterior

In addition, the pathologic appearing compression fracture of T12 is stable.

1.  No evidence of intra-abdominal or retroperitoneal hematoma.

2.  New soft tissue nodules and soft tissue changes along the anterior
abdominal wall.  Please correlate with site of injections.

should be followed with a CT in 3 months to assure resolution given the
patient's malignancy history.
